# firecrawl crawl

Bulk extract content from a website. Crawls pages following links up to a depth/limit.

**Prerequisite:** `crawl` requires authentication (no keyless free tier); without credentials the CLI prompts an interactive login.

## Quick start

```bash
# Crawl a docs section
firecrawl crawl "<url>" --include-paths /docs --limit 50 --wait -o .firecrawl/crawl.json

# Full crawl with depth limit
firecrawl crawl "<url>" --max-depth 3 --wait --progress -o .firecrawl/crawl.json

# Check status of a running crawl
firecrawl crawl <job-id>
```

Run `firecrawl crawl --help` for the full option list.

**Done when:** the crawl reaches a terminal status and the saved output under `.firecrawl/` contains the expected pages.

## Tips

- Use `--wait` when you need the results immediately. It has no default timeout; use `--timeout <seconds>` to bound polling. Without `--wait`, crawl returns a job ID for async polling.
- **One crawl, not a scrape loop.** If you're about to scrape a third page from the same site or section, crawl it instead with `--limit`.
- **Scope crawls with `--include-paths`** whenever the request names a section — crawl only the pages you need.
- Crawl consumes credits per page. Check `firecrawl credit-usage` before large crawls (`credit-usage` requires authentication).

## See also

- [firecrawl-scrape](../firecrawl-scrape/SKILL.md) — scrape individual pages
- [firecrawl-map](../firecrawl-map/SKILL.md) — discover URLs before deciding to crawl
- [firecrawl-download](../firecrawl-download/SKILL.md) — download site to local files (uses map + scrape)
- [firecrawl-build-scrape](https://github.com/firecrawl/skills/tree/main/skills/build/firecrawl-build-scrape) — building bulk extraction into an app instead of running it here

I crawled `https://docs.firecrawl.dev/features` with a 10-page limit and got 10 pages. The raw output is saved at `/tmp/fceval-s07-t1-6rbt5xic/work/.firecrawl/crawl.json`.

1. **/features** (the index page): The crawler returned content about single sign-on (SSO) with SAML or OIDC and SCIM directory sync. These are enterprise features enabled per organization. The page's links point to `/features/sso`, so this looks like the SSO page rather than a features overview.
2. **/features/llm-extract**: JSON mode on `/scrape` pulls structured fields from a single URL. For multiple URLs or discovery, the page points you to Agent.
3. **/features/ask**: `/support/ask` is an AI support agent exposed as an API. It returns a verified diagnosis with fix parameters in about 15–30 seconds, and it's aimed mainly at AI agent callers.
4. **/features/pii-redaction**: Setting `redactPII: true` on a scrape request replaces personally identifiable information in the returned markdown. This lets you pass the output safely to agents, logs, vector stores or analytics.
5. **/features/threat-protection**: Your organization can block Firecrawl from fetching risky URLs. Every URL a request would fetch is checked against your policy, and URLs that fail are refused.
6. **/features/alpha/deep-research**: This is a legacy v1 deep-research API that is being deprecated in favor of the Search API and the Deep Research use case. The endpoint stays active but is no longer maintained.
7. **/features/crawl**: Crawl recursively discovers and scrapes every reachable subpage, using sitemaps and link traversal. It supports path filters, depth limits and subdomain or external-link control, and it returns markdown or structured data per page.
8. **/features/research**: Firecrawl Research is a search index of about 43 million paper abstracts, mostly biomedical and life sciences, for research agents. It has tools for searching papers, reading metadata and full-text passages, and finding related papers.
9. **/features/scrape**: Scrape turns a web page into clean markdown, structured data, screenshots or HTML. It handles proxies, caching, rate limits, JS-rendered pages, PDFs and images.
10. **/features/agent**: `/agent` takes a goal and autonomously searches and navigates the web when you don't know the URLs. For a single known URL, JSON mode on `/scrape` is cheaper.

Two of the crawled URLs came back with tracking query strings (`?m=fire573-copilot-cowork-...`), which I ignored. I wrote the summaries from the opening of each page, not the full text.
